messages.content: Estou planejando um acampamento e preciso saber a previsão do tempo. Você pode me buscar os dados meteorológicos do acampamento localizado para os próximos 10 dias, incluindo previsões diárias de temperatura e precipitação? Além disso, prefiro a temperatura máxima de 2 minutos em Fahrenheit e a soma da precipitação em polegadas.

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

The user wants weather forecast for a camping location for next 10 days, including daily temperature and precipitation. They prefer maximum temperature at 2-minute resolution in Fahrenheit and sum of precipitation in inches. We need to fetch data from Open-Meteo API. But we need coordinates. The user didn't provide location. We need to ask for coordinates or location name. We can ask for latitude and longitude. Also note that Open-Meteo API supports hourly data, but not 2-minute resolution. Actually Open-Meteo provides 1-hourly data. There's also "Open-Meteo 2-minute" API? I think there's an "Open-Meteo 2-minute" endpoint: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=...&longitude=...&hourly=temperature_2m,precipitation&forecast_days=10. But 2-minute resolution might not be available. There's "Open-Meteo 2-minute" API: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=...&longitude=...&hourly=temperature_2m,precipitation&forecast_days=10&timeformat=unixtime. But 2-minute resolution is not standard. There's "Open-Meteo 2-minute" API: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=...&longitude=...&hourly=temperature_2m,precipitation&forecast_days=10&interval=2min. Actually there is "Open-Meteo 2-minute" API: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=...&longitude=...&hourly=temperature_2m,precipitation&forecast_days=10&interval=2min. Let's check. The Open-Meteo API has "hourly" and "daily" parameters. For 2-minute resolution, there's "hourly" but you can specify "interval=2min" to get 2-minute data. According to docs, you can use "hourly=temperature_2m,precipitation" and "interval=2min". So we can request 2-minute data. Then we can compute daily max temperature and sum precipitation. We need to convert temperature to Fahrenheit. Precipitation is in mm, we need to convert to inches. 1 inch = 25.4 mm. So sum precipitation in mm then divide by 25.4.

We need to ask for latitude and longitude. Also we need to confirm if they want daily max temperature at 2-minute resolution. That means we need to compute daily max from 2-minute data. We can do that after retrieving data. But we can also request daily max temperature directly from API: daily=temperature_2m_max. But that gives daily max at hourly resolution. But we want 2-minute resolution. So we need to compute ourselves. So we need to request hourly data at 2-minute resolution. Then compute daily max and sum precipitation. So we need to ask for coordinates. Also we need to ask for timezone? The API returns times in UTC by default. We can specify timezone=auto to get local timezone. So we can request timezone=auto.

Thus we need to ask user for latitude and longitude. Also we need to ask for timezone? We can set timezone=auto. So we can ask for coordinates. Then we can call the function.

We need to produce a function call. The function signature: requests_get with url, headers, timeout, params, etc. We'll call with url: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast". Params: latitude, longitude, hourly=temperature_2m,precipitation, interval=2min, forecast_days=10, timezone=auto. We can set headers default. So we need to ask for coordinates first.
